This is fun to play with, however, one should know the difference between this and VSCO presets. The difference being every. single. camera. is different so applying THESE to photos from cameras of different manufacturers will produce vastly different results. The value of VSCO is they match their presets to each camera raw. So, if you're like me and shoot a Fuji x100 and a Nikon d800, applying VSCO's filters to each one will produce near identical toning. Applying these to each will provide much different results. VSCO's value is accuracy and, for me, that's a big deal. I shoot a hella ton of film (a few rolls a week) and when I use VSCO it's to help any digital files flow in the same toning/grading as my film scans. The less I have to fiddle with that, the better. As someone who shoots a ton of film, VSCO's emulation for each specific camera (I've tested on Nikon, Fuji, and Leica) are pretty amazingly great emulations!

Not saying these presets are bad, but just wanted to point out that they are not a VSCO replacement.
